vocabulary.meaning_en: a sudden dangerous situation that needs fast action
vocabulary.example: In an emergency, stay calm and follow the instructions.

vocabulary.meaning_en: suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly
a practice of what to do in an emergency
vocabulary.example: That was just a fire drill, not a real fire.

vocabulary.meaning_en: doing something to get ready for the real thing
vocabulary.note_ar: في بريطانيا practice اسم وpractise فعل
vocabulary.example: The drill is a practice for a real fire.
Please leave the building by the nearest exit.

vocabulary.meaning_en: steps that go from one floor to another
vocabulary.example: Use the stairs, not the lift.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a machine that carries people between floors
vocabulary.note_ar: lift في بريطانيا، elevator في أمريكا
vocabulary.note_en: Lift is British; elevator is American.
vocabulary.example: Never use the lift during a fire.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not here; we cannot find them
become the person who controls a situation
vocabulary.example: When the manager was out, Anna took charge.

vocabulary.meaning_en: listening to or looking at something carefully
vocabulary.example: Could I have your attention, please?

vocabulary.meaning_en: the grey cloud that comes from something burning

vocabulary.example: Tom put out the fire in the warehouse.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a brave person who helps others
vocabulary.example: The man who saved his colleague was a hero.

vocabulary.meaning_en: if something that probably won't happen does happen (formal)
vocabulary.note_en: A formal phrase used in instructions.
vocabulary.example: In the unlikely event of a fire, use the stairs.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a very bad situation because of a mistake
vocabulary.example: He is in serious trouble for breaking the rules.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the most important boss of the company
vocabulary.example: The head of the company is visiting today.

fine_lines.title: lift vs elevator
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمتان بمعنى المصعد؛ lift بريطانية وelevator أمريكية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean the machine that carries people up and down. Lift is British, elevator is American.

examples.sentence: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
The elevator is next to reception.

fine_lines.title: stairs vs steps
fine_lines.explanation_ar: stairs هي السلالم داخل المبنى بين الطوابق، وsteps درجات قليلة غالبًا خارج المبنى أو كل درجة منفردة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Stairs go between floors inside a building. Steps are single steps, often a few outside a door.

examples.sentence: Walk down the stairs to the ground floor.
There are three steps at the front door.

fine_lines.title: anybody vs nobody
fine_lines.explanation_ar: anybody في الأسئلة والنفي (Is anybody missing?)، وnobody تعني لا أحد وتأتي مع فعل مثبت.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use anybody in questions and negatives. Nobody means 'no person' and goes with a positive verb.

examples.sentence: Nobody is missing. Everyone is here.

expressions.example: There's no need to panic. Everything is under control.

expressions.phrase: Please leave the building and meet outside.
expressions.meaning_ar: يُرجى مغادرة المبنى والتجمع في الخارج.
expressions.meaning_en: Go out and wait outside together.
expressions.example: The alarm is ringing. Please leave the building and meet outside.

expressions.phrase: Use the stairs not the lift.
expressions.meaning_en: Do not take the lift in a fire.
expressions.example: Use the stairs not the lift, and walk calmly.
We're all outside now. Is anybody missing?

expressions.phrase: Could I have your attention, please?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنني أن أحظى بانتباهكم من فضلكم؟
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask people to listen.
expressions.example: Could I have your attention, please? We need to leave now.
Please stay calm and follow me.

expressions.meaning_en: It was a practice, not a real emergency.
expressions.example: Don't worry, that was just a drill.

grammar.title: Giving instructions politely: Please + imperative
grammar.explanation_ar: لإعطاء تعليمات مهذبة في الطوارئ نضع please قبل فعل الأمر: Please leave the building. ونستخدم Use ... not ... لبيان البديل الصحيح.
grammar.explanation_en: Put please before an imperative to give polite instructions: Please leave the building. Use 'X not Y' to show the right choice.
examples: Use the stairs not the lift.

grammar.title: There's no need to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم There's no need to + فعل مجرد لنقول إن شيئًا ما غير ضروري، وهي طريقة لطيفة لتهدئة الناس.
grammar.explanation_en: Use There's no need to + base verb to say something is not necessary. It is a kind way to calm people.
examples: There's no need to call me back.

questions.question: What can you say to keep people calm?
questions.explanation_ar: There's no need to panic تعني لا داعي للذعر.
questions.explanation_en: This phrase tells people not to be afraid.

questions.question: Use the ___ not the lift.
questions.explanation_en: In a fire, use the stairs.

questions.question: "Is anybody ___?" (Is everyone here?)
questions.explanation_en: Missing is the adjective meaning 'not here'.

questions.question: Which word is American English for 'lift'?
Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: التركيب الصحيح: There's no need to + فعل.
questions.explanation_en: The pattern is There's no need to + verb.

questions.question: "Take charge" means...
questions.explanation_en: Take charge means become the leader in a situation.

questions.question: Tom ___ the fire in the warehouse.
questions.explanation_ar: put out a fire تعني أطفأ الحريق.
questions.explanation_en: Put out a fire means stop it burning.

questions.question: Which is a polite instruction?
questions.explanation_ar: Please + فعل الأمر طريقة مهذبة للتعليمات.
questions.explanation_en: Please + imperative is a polite instruction.
